be using a gross amount of memory (> 10G).  I've seen some posts
about this from back in March and I'm just wondering what the status
of it is.

I think one of my problems is that I didn't set it to the 'core' set
for the human exon array, so maybe that would help somewhat.

Cheers,
Mark

"utils"

other attached packages:
            GLAD              aws aroma.affymetrix           digest
        "1.10.0"          "1.3-2"          "0.5.2"          "0.3.0"
       aroma.apd           R.huge      aroma.light          affyPLM
         "0.1.3"          "0.1.4"          "1.4.1"         "1.12.0"
           gcrma      matchprobes         affydata             affy
         "2.8.1"          "1.8.1"         "1.11.2"         "1.14.1"
          affyio          Biobase       affxparser         R.native
         "1.4.0"         "1.14.0"          "1.8.0"          "0.1.2"
           R.rsp          R.cache          R.utils             R.oo
         "0.3.3"          "0.1.5"          "0.9.5"          "1.2.8"

I think the problem arose in 'fromFiles.ChipEffectSet', because the
argument 'checkChipType' is passed to 'fromFiles.AffymetrixCelSet'
twice, once when
'clazz$fromFiles(path = getPath(this), checkChipType = FALSE)'
is called by 'getOutputDataSet.Transform', and once from
'fromFiles.ChipEffectSet'. The former is wrapped up in the '...'
argument and the latter is explicit.

When I added 'checkChipType' as an argument, it all worked OK :

setMethodS3("fromFiles", "ChipEffectSet", function(static,
path="plmData/", pattern=",chipEffects[.](c|C)(e|E)(l|L)
$", ...,checkChipType = FALSE, fileClass=NULL) {
  # Argument 'fileClass':
  if (is.null(fileClass))
    fileClass <- gsub("Set$", "File", class(static)[1]);

  # Unfortunately does method dispatching not work here.
  fromFiles.AffymetrixCelSet(static, path=path, pattern=pattern, ...,
fileClass=fileClass, checkChipType=checkChipType);
}, static=TRUE)

>   cesN <- process(fln, verbose=log)

RAM: 0.02MB
Parameters: (probeModel: chr "pm", mergeStrands: logi TRUE,
combineAlleles: logi TRUE)

Otherwise things have been running smoothly so far with this version.

Thanks,

Jeremy

messages.body_plain:
Hello

I have a regions.xls file after analysing 10K snp chip files and just
wanted to confirm that I am looking at the correct genome build.

In this file are columns headed 'Chromosome' 'start' 'stop' and 'url'

'url' references hg17, e.g.
http://genome.ucsc.edu/cgi-bin/hgTracks?clade=vertebrate&org=Human&db=hg17&position=chr5%:38217727-42101341
so I would assume that the Chromosome, start and stop columns, which
differ from the coordinates in the url entry, refer to hg18, e.g.
the url mentioned above is on the same line as:
Chromosome	start	stop
5	40,067,067	40,252,001

I am just checking as I did a liftOver on the coordinates in the url
(from hg17 to hg18) and that didn't give me the region under the
'Chromosome, start, stop' entry.

cheers

Lavinia.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Lavinia.

On 7/1/07, Lavinia Gordon <lavinia...@mcri.edu.au> wrote:
>
> Hello
>
> I have a regions.xls file after analysing 10K snp chip files and just
> wanted to confirm that I am looking at the correct genome build.
>
> In this file are columns headed 'Chromosome' 'start' 'stop' and 'url'
>
> 'url' references hg17, e.g.
> http://genome.ucsc.edu/cgi-bin/hgTracks?clade=vertebrate&org=Human&db=hg17&position=chr5%:38217727-42101341
> so I would assume that the Chromosome, start and stop columns, which
> differ from the coordinates in the url entry, refer to hg18, e.g.
> the url mentioned above is on the same line as:
> Chromosome      start   stop
> 5       40,067,067      40,252,001

The '<xlim[1]>-<xlim[2]>' in the URL string, e.g. '38217727-42101341',
specifies *the region to be displayed* and is calculated as:

start <- 40067067
stop <- 40252001
width <- abs(stop-start)
margin <- 10
xlim <- c(max(start - margin*width, 0), stop + margin*width);

which explains why 'xlim' is different from 'c(start, stop)'.

>
> I am just checking as I did a liftOver on the coordinates in the url
> (from hg17 to hg18) and that didn't give me the region under the
> 'Chromosome, start, stop' entry.

I have hardwired 'hg17' in the URL, that is, the genome version is
currently not inferred from anywhere.  The genome version used is the
one used to create the dChip genome information file, e.g.
10K_Xba142_genome_info_hg17.xls.  This far I don't think dChip provide
genome information files for other genome versions than 'hg17'.  If
that happens, the URL will still say 'hg17' (until I come up with
clever and safe way to infer the version number).

Cheers

Henrik

>
> cheers
>
> Lavinia.
>
>
> >

messages.subject_clean: [aroma.affymetrix] firma status?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mark,

does it increase linearly with the number of arrays?  I checked the
code in fit() of the FirmaModel and I think it because each of the
FIRMA score files caches the results.

If you run fit() for the first, say 5 arrays, then I suspect that you
will see that the objectSize() of the first 5 FirmaFile:s will be
large than for the non-fitted ones.  Example:

 fs <- getFirmaScores(firma);
 fit(firma, verbose=-8)
 <Break after 5 arrays>
 for (kk in 1:10) print(objectSize(getFile(fs, kk)))

I've fixed this and uploaded a patch.  So, do:

library(aroma.affymetrix)
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix")

and let me know if it helps.

Cheers

Henrik

Hi Yifang,

you are raising a few different issues here.  Let's first solve the

>

> But after I run plm <- ExonRmaPlm(csN, mergeGroups=TRUE)
> The R crashed under windows but it's running under unix.

Could you clarify what you mean by R crashes on Windows?  Does R just
die or do you get an error message?  I assume it is not in the
declaration of ExonRmaPlm, but rather when you run fit(plm), correct?
Add argument fit(plm, verbose=-8), and cut'n'paste what you get when
the error occurs/or what you got before R dies.

Look also at the outputs from the garbage collection, which will give
you an indication of the memory usage.  I don't have the CDF for chip
type MoEx-1_0-st-v1 so I cannot really tell how memory intensive it
is.  If you find that you are using a lot of memory, more than the
1.5GB that your Windows machine has, you'll be swapping a lot and that
will slow down everything substantially.  You can the add argument
fit(plm, ram=0.20, verbose=-8) to fit chunks of 20% of the default
size.  You should be able to fit any data set of any size.

BTW, read/write will be quite much faster if you work of a local disk
rather than of a shared file system, especially if the shared one is
slow or heavily used.

messages.body_plain:
Ok, now we found where the crash occurs.  It is when aroma.affymetrix
tries to query the CDF for cell indices.  From your previous messages,
I see that you have:

> cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("MoEx-1_0-st-v1")
> print(cdf)
AffymetrixCdfFile:
Path: annotationData/chipTypes/MoEx-1_0-st-v1
Filename: MoEx-1_0-st-v1.cdf
Filesize: 740.05MB
Chip type: MoEx-1_0-st-v1
Dimension: 2560x2560
Number of cells: 6553600
Number of units: 1257006
Cells per unit: 5.21
Number of QC units: 0
RAM: 0.00MB

so at least the *header* information of the CDF and the file size
seems to be alright.  However, somehow there is a problem when
querying the *data section* of the CDF.  Aroma.affymetrix is using
affxparser for all this, so it is actually affxparser, or more
precisely the Affymetrix Fusion SDK library it uses that causes the
crash).  Unfortunately, there is no sophisticated exception handling
in Fusion SDK meaning we cannot really catch exception and because of
this it might lead to crashes like yours.  It is rare, but it happens.
 For example, trying to read an empty (zero bytes) CDF file, used to
crash R, but then we added a test in R for this case.  However, say
that the CDF is only 80% of the real size, say, due to a failed
copying, then we can't control for that.

So, that's the explanation for the crash.  Now let's troubleshoot.

1) Identify a simple case where it crashes.  I think the following will do:

pathname <- getPathname(cdf)
cdf <- readCdfCellIndices(pathname, units=NULL)

You may even try reading a single unit, e.g.

cdf <- readCdfCellIndices(pathname, units=654123)

and see if that crash.

2) You said you are running of the local file system on Windows and on
the shared on Unix, where it works.  Make sure that the two copies of
the MoEx-1_0-st-v1.CDF file are of identical sizes.  You can do this
by:

pathname <- getPathname(cdf)
file.info <http://file.info>(pathname)$size

If they are of identical sizes, then verify that their contents are
identical by comparing the output of:

pathname <- getPathname(cdf)
digest(pathname, file=TRUE)

You should get a 32-character hexadecimal (MD5) string, e.g.
"11f8b05ed782aa400e467da99d49c558".

If they are identical on Windows and Unix, move to the next step.

3) Above it says the CDF is 740.05MB.  This is so large so I suspect
you have an ASCII version of the CDF.  You will be much much much^10
better off if you work with a binary CDF instead.  The IO will be many
times faster.  This could also explain the slow performance on Unix.
It might also explain why it crashes on Windows; affxparser/Fusion SDK
may simply run out of memory.  You can convert a CDF from ASCII to
binary, using convertCdf() in the affxparser package.  See ?convertCdf
for more details.  Archive the ASCII version somewhere and replace it
with new binary CDF.  When you do print(cdf) on the new CDF, you
should see that the file size is much smaller, around 50-80 MB.

4) Using the binary CDF, retry Step 1 and see if it crashes.

Cheers

/Henrik

Hi.

Sorry, getAbsolutePath() is in the R.utils package.  Anyway, the
pathname does not seem to be the problem.

Let's try to find a minimal example where it crash.  From previous
messages I though the following code crashes R for you - can you
confirm it does?

library(aroma.affymetrix)
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("MoEx-1_0-st-v1")

pathname <- getPathname(cdf)
cells <- readCdfCellIndices(pathname, units=654123, verbose=2)

If not, does this one do it?

cells <- readCdfCellIndices(pathname, units=NULL, verbose=2)

The latter uses about 450MB of RAM to load.

BTW, do you run a fresh R session, that is, do you normally save your
R sessions or do you always start from scratch?  What does ls() and
gc() report immediately after you start R?

-H

Hi,

and with what packages loaded.  Let's start over and could you please
write each of your replies immediately after each of my
questions/comments, e.g.

> HB: Do you do foo?

No, I do bar.

...and so on.

We need to identify a minimal set of code that causes R to crash for
you.  So, below is what I want you to do. I need to see the output for
all items with an asterisk (*), although we done some of the before.
For the long outputs of loops you my remove the repetitive
intermediate lines.  If it crashes I only need to know that it crash,
and any of the output before it crashes.  Also, if it crashes, try the
same step many times to see if it happens every time.

0*) Assert that you and I got a different affxparser installation:
  dll <- system.file("libs/affxparser.dll", package="affxparser")
  print(dll)
  print(digest::digest(dll, file=TRUE))

1) Start a fresh R session, and load only the affxparser package,
because I suspect this is a problem with affxparser and not with
aroma.affymetrix et al.

2) Change the working directory to the directory where the CDF lives, e.g.
  path <- "C:/Documents and
Settings/hu/aroma/trial1/annotationData/chipTypes/MoEx-1_0-st-v1/"
  setwd(path)

3*) Assert that the CDF is readable:
  hdr <- readCdfHeader("MoEx-1_0-st-v1.cdf")
  print(hdr)

4*) Trying to read the parts of the CDF:

    cells <- readCdfCellIndices("MoEx-1_0-st-v1.cdf", units=1)

    str(cells)
    cells <- readCdfCellIndices("MoEx-1_0-st-v1.cdf", units=654123)
    str(cells)

6*) Trying to read the complete CDF:
    cells <- readCdfCellIndices("MoEx-1_0-st-v1.cdf", units=NULL)
    str(cells)

7*) Trying to read the complete CDF in chunks:
  hdr <- readCdfHeader("MoEx-1_0-st-v1.cdf")
  units <- matrix(1:hdr$nunits, nrow=3282)
  str(units)
  for (cc in 1:ncol(units)) {
    cat(sprintf("iteration=%3d, first=%6d, len=%d\n", cc, units[1,cc],
length(units)))
    cells <- readCdfCellIndices("MoEx-1_0-st-v1.cdf", units=units[,cc])
  }
  cat("done!\n")

8*) Stress test:
  hdr <- readCdfHeader("MoEx-1_0-st-v1.cdf")
  for (cc in 1:100) {
    len <- sample(0.10*hdr$nunits, size=1)
    units <- sort(sample(hdr$nunits, size=len))
    cat(sprintf("iteration=%3d, first=%6d, len=%d\n", cc, units[1],
length(units)))
    cells <- readCdfCellIndices("MoEx-1_0-st-v1.cdf", units=units)
  }
  cat("done!\n")

/Henrik

Hi,

I don't know what to say - I was in some sense hoping to see a crash
;)  Ok, now lets try loading aroma.affymetrix and doing almost the
same but now not setting the working directory.  Honestly, I cannot
see how this would make a difference, but the other day you reported
that R crashed under such conditions.

# 1) Start a fresh R session and now load aroma.affymetrix
library(aroma.affymetrix)

# 2*) Locate the CDF

cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("MoEx-1_0-st-v1")

pathname <- getPathname(cdf)
print(pathname)

# 3*) Assert that the CDF is readable:
hdr <- readCdfHeader(pathname)
print(hdr)

# 4*) Trying to read the parts of the CDF:
cells <- readCdfCellIndices(pathname, units=1)
str(cells)
cells <- readCdfCellIndices(pathname, units=654123)
str(cells)

# 5*) Trying to read the complete CDF:
cells <- readCdfCellIndices(pathname, units=NULL)
str(cells[1:10])

# 6*) Stress test:
hdr <- readCdfHeader(pathname)

for (cc in 1:100) {
  len <- sample(0.10*hdr$nunits, size=1)
  units <- sort(sample(hdr$nunits, size=len))
  cat(sprintf("iteration=%3d, first=%6d, len=%d\n", cc, units[1],
length(units)))

  cells <- readCdfCellIndices(pathname, units=units)
}
cat("done!\n")

/Henrik

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Querying CDF crashes R on Windows (Was: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: summarization speedP)
messages.subject_clean: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Querying CDF crashes R on Windows (Was: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: summarization speedP)
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

some updates on the trickiest troubleshooting this far.  FYI, Yifang
sent me the data files off-line so I could test the same script on my
WinXP machine.  I finally manage to reproduce the crash.  It happens
when the affxparser tries to read a corrupt CDF file, which causes the
underlying Fusion SDK library to crash/core dump.

Here is a likely scenario of what happened:

1) When aroma.affymetrix fits a probe-level model, it stores the
results in CEL files that have a structure similar to the original
files, but with only one cell (probe) per unit (probeset).  The CDF
that describes these files layout are called monocell CDFs, e.g.
MoEx-1_0-st-v1,monocell.CDF.  Monocell CDFs are created "on the fly"
(2-60 mins) from the original CDF, if missing.  This is only done once
per CDF.

2) The MoEx-1_0-st-v1.CDF has a large number of units (>1.2M!).  A
confounded effect of one piece of internal code in the affxparser
package not being optimized for memory usage plus the fact that Yifang
used an ASCII version of CDF, which takes up even more memory, caused
the R session on Windows XP (1.5GB RAM) to run out of memory while
creating the monocell CDF, leaving an incomplete
MoEx-1_0-st-v1,monocell.CDF sitting there.  [I managed to reproduce
this on my machine too].

3) When aroma.affymetrix was restarted and tries to fit the PLM again,
it located the monocell CDF and thinks everything is fine.  However,
when it tries to query it via affxparser R crash, and so on.

I've updated aroma.affymetrix (I'll send out an update soon) so that
the monocell CDF is created as a temporary file, e.g.
MoEx-1_0-st-v1,monocell.CDF.tmp, which if successfully completed and
validated, will be renamed to MoEx-1_0-st-v1,monocell.CDF.  This will
make it more robust against scenarios as the above.  The update also
contains a patch to make affxparser much more memory efficient.

So, Yifang, 1) update aroma.affymetrix (see next email),  2) have a
look at the file size of the monocell CDF you have on your WinXP
machine and compare it to the one you have on Unix; they are probably
different.  3) Remove the incomplete MoEx-1_0-st-v1,monocell.CDF, and
restart your analysis.  If it for some reason complains about a
*missing* monocell CDF, you can create it explicitly by:

cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("MoEx-1_0-st-v1")

createMonoCell(cdf, verbose=-50),

Note, this exon chip got so many units so this will take 30-50 minutes
to generate the monocell CDF.  I've reran your script with the updated
aroma.affymetrix and everything went well.

Cheers

/Henrik

This is unfortunately nothing we can prevent, but we can at least try
to avoid getting corrupt CDF files from the beginning.

messages.subject: aroma.affymetrix v0.5.3 released
messages.subject_clean: aroma.affymetrix v0.5.3 released
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

aroma.affymetrix v0.5.3 is now available.  It solves the issues
recently discussed on group list.    Here are the changes:

Version: 0.5.3 [2007-07-13]
o Package passes R CMD check on Rv2.5.1 (and R v2.6.0 devel).
o Package passes all (#1 and #2) redundancy test sets available on
  the group page.  This was confirmed on R v2.5.1 on WinXP (1.5GB RAM).
o Now more verbose output is generated when a monocell CDF is created
  in the background.
o Added getFileFormat() to AffymetrixCdfFile and AffymetrixCelFile.
  These are also reported by the corresponding print() method.
o Made bgAdjustOptical(), bgAdjustRma(), and bgAdjustGcRma() deprecated.
  If used, an error will be thrown.  Use the Optical-, Rma-, and
  GcRmaBackgroundCorrection classes instead.
o MEMORY OPTIMIZATION:  Includes a patch to affxparser:::.initializeCdf()
  to make it much more memory efficient, e.g. when writing the CDF
  header unit names, it could consume >1.5GB RAM, whereas now it is
  in the order of 100-200MB.  This patch will go away as soon as
  the affxparser package incorporates it.
o MEMORY OPTIMIZATION:  Includes a patch to base::matrix() that does not
  create an extra copy when assigned a new value to a cell, e.g. the 2nd
  statement in the following would force a new copy of the matrix:
  x <- matrix(0, 5000,5000); x[1,1] <- 1;  Thanks to Luke Tierney for
  troubleshooting and suggesting a patch; there are no immediate plans
  to include this patch in 'base' though.
o BUG FIX: Now (private) createMonoCell() of AffymetrixCdfFile will
  build the monocell CDF to a temporary filename, and only when it is
  done, rename it to the final *,monocell.cdf filename.  This will
  lower the risk for creating an invalid CDF, which for instance can
  happen if we run out of memory.  Reading invalid CDFs will core
  dump R due to the affxparser and the Fusion SDK package.
o BUG FIX: The memory usage of fit() of the FirmaModel would increase
  linearly with the number of arrays processed.  This was because
  read results where cached for each of the FirmaFile:s.  Thanks Mark
  Robinson for reporting on this.
o BUG FIX: getOutputDataSet() of Transform would give "Error in
  fromFiles.AffymetrixCelSet(static, path = path, pattern = pattern,:
  formal argument "checkChipType" matched by multiple actual arguments".
  This was due to the recent adding of 'checkChipType=FALSE'.  Fixed
  by adding 'checkChipType=FALSE' to fromFiles() of ChipEffectSet.
  Thanks Jeremy Silver at WEHI for report and troubleshooting this.

See group page for instructions how to update.  Any patches previously
downloaded will be deleted automatically.

/Henrik

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Problem of RmaBackgroundCorrection in new aroma.affymetrix release
messages.subject_clean: [aroma.affymetrix] Problem of RmaBackgroundCorrection in new aroma.affymetrix release
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Both RmaBackgroundCorrection and QuantileNormalization are so called
Transform classes (inheriting from this superclass).  When you define
objects of these, e.g. via constructor RmaBackgroundCorrection(), you
will only setup a Transform object, but you will not perform any
preprocessing.  In order to do this, you have to call the process()
method which returns a transformed AffymetrixCelSet, which is what you
want.

Please see subsection "Calibration and normalization of probe-level
data" under "Pages" on the aroma.affymetrix group site.  See also the
examples.

Cheers

Henrik

As you see, it works well and the memory overhead is minimal.  I

problem when one runs out of memory, or that your main CDF is corrupt
(failed to convert to binary or something).

More comments below.

On 7/16/07, Yifang Hu <h...@wehi.edu.au> wrote:
>
> Hi Henrik,
>
> Thanks. It's working now. However, I've another problem. Sorry.
> There is error when access the cel data.
> My code and output are listed below. Did I do something wrong?

Not directly, but you should rather use [[ instead of [ if you're
querying a single unit, but that is not the reason for the error.

> But it's working under unix when using the previous version.

Hmm... It is working on Unix on a previous aroma.affymetrix version
and on copies of the above files.

1) I don't think that the new version of aroma.affymetrix made any
difference, but it is good to know if you see same problem on Unix
with the updated version.

2) More importantly, validate your CDF files against the one on Unix.
Are you using the binary or the ASCII version and the same on Unix and
Windows?

3) The error message you receive is from affxparser and says there is
a problem reading the CDF (it typically means that it cannot open the
file in the first place).  Start a fresh R session and do:

> verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-50)
> timestampOn(verbose)
> cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("MICE_2007", chipType="MoEx-1_0-st-v1")
> cdf <- getCdf(cs)
> print(cdf)
> str(readUnits(cdf, units=1))

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

there certainly seems to some memory issues, as the error message
says.  I guess this is due to the layout of the exon arrays, i.e.
there are some units with a very-large number of probes (although I
haven't verified this).  Try setting the 'ram' argument of fit() to a
smaller than number than the default 1, e.g.

  fit(plm, ram=0.3, verbose=verbose).

That should do.  Already fitted units should not be refitted.

Cheers

Henrik

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

this is most likely related to what Ken noticed for the human exon
array where for instance one unit has ~17000 probes(!), cf.

  http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/optimization-speed-file-space-ram

The fitting time grows exponentially(?) with the number of
probes/chips.  Thus, for such large units alternative
modelling/algorithms have to be found.  I do not know of any work that
attacks this problem.

Cheers

Henrik

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Failed to subset a CEL set (Was: Re: Querying CDF crashes R on Windows)
messages.subject_clean: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Failed to subset a CEL set (Was: Re: Querying CDF crashes R on Windows)
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

yes try to restart.  It never hurts to restart - also,
aroma.affymetrix remembers what's already processed and skips that.
Also try a smaller 'ram' value if it happens again.

Again, when you see "Failed to read the CDF file." that message comes
from affxparser and is because its internal Affymetrix Fusion SDK
library fails to initiate the CDF for reading, which in turn (from our
recent experience) is likely to happen when you run out of memory.

Operation system crash course: R runs as a *process* in Windows/Unix.
All memory allocation by R, its packages and the packages internal
library is done in the process shared memory.  If some of the code
fails to clean up the memory, the only way to get that memory back is
to terminate the process, that is, to terminate R and start a new R
session.  R itself and packages written in plain R, such as
aroma.affymetrix et al, utilizes the built in R garbage collector to
clean out the memory and there should be no issues with that one.  My
*guess* is that Fusion SDK does not deallocate the memory allocated
when it runs out of memory; meaning there are allocated memory blocks
that won't be freed until you restart R.

/H

Henrik Bengtsson wrote:
> Hi,
>
> Both RmaBackgroundCorrection and QuantileNormalization are so called
> Transform classes (inheriting from this superclass).  When you define
> objects of these, e.g. via constructor RmaBackgroundCorrection(), you
> will only setup a Transform object, but you will not perform any
> preprocessing.  In order to do this, you have to call the process()
> method which returns a transformed AffymetrixCelSet, which is what you
> want.
>
> Please see subsection "Calibration and normalization of probe-level
> data" under "Pages" on the aroma.affymetrix group site.  See also the
> examples.
>
> Cheers
>
> Henrik
>
> On 7/17/07, jhanre...@gmail.com <jhanre...@gmail.com> wrote:
> >
> > Hi,
> >
> > I met a problem of using RmaBackgroundCorrection in the new release.
> > In the pase, I was using the following code to process the exon array
> > data, and it works well:
> > ds <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("GBM", chipType="HuEx-1_0-st-v2");
> > cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("HuEx-1_0-st-v2,full");
> > setCdf(ds, cdf);
> > dsBG <- bgAdjustRma(ds, name=getName(ds),
> > path=file.path("probeData",getName(ds), "RMABG"), addJitter=TRUE,
> > verbose=-2);
> > qn <- QuantileNormalization(dsBG, typesToUpdate="pm");
> >
> > As the bgAdjustRma() was deprecated is the new version, I used the

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Some questions about plotting and normalization
messages.subject_clean: [aroma.affymetrix] Some questions about plotting and normalization
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jeremy.

On 7/4/07, Jeremy Silver <sil...@wehi.edu.au> wrote:
>
> Hi Henrik,
>
> I'm writing out parts of my honours thesis and I'd like to include a
> short description about each of the preprocessing steps I've done. I
> have a few questions:
>
> 1) How can I make figures similar to those at the top of the 'PCR
> fragment length normalization' page? If there's some special command,
> I couldn't find it either searching through the group pages or through
> the source code.

No special command (it's on the wish list to generate reports
containing such but that wont happen anytime soon).

The base for those (PMA,PMB) plots before and after crosstalk
calibration is geneplotter::smoothScatter() where I've highlighted the
fitted crosstalk parameters as thick lines.

You can fit the crosstalk model by calling fit <- fitGenotypeCone(y)
explicitly where y is a two-column matrix where each row contains
(PMA,PMB).  See ?fitGenotypeCone.matrix (and the source code) to see
what is returned so that you can draw the lines too.  After fitting
the model, you calibrate 'y' by calling yC <-
backtransformGenotypeCone(y, fit=fit).

In order to stratify on nucleotide pairs, e.g. (A,T), you first have
to identify what units interrogate such probe pairs.  You can use
affxparser::readCdfGroupNames() to find such information, because the
unit group names indicate the nucleotide for the alleles.  When you
know which these units are, you can use
affxparser::readCdfCellIndices() to get the cell (probe) indices of
these probes.  Note that you have to take special care of the probe
pairs on the anti-sense strand by swapping their cell indices such
that (T,A) becomes (A,T).  Then you can model sense and anti-sense
together (as done by CRMA).  With the cell indices, you can use for
instance affxparser::readCelIntensities() and matrix() to obtain 'y'.

Hope this helps.

>
> 2) The 'Calibration and normalization of probe-level data' page
> describes optical background correction, fragment length normalization
> and allelic cross-talk normalization. The example analyses (both CN
> and exon array analysis) use only the fragment length normalization.
> Can you say a few words about when you'd recommend using background
> correction or allelic cross-talk normalization? If I'm correctly
> informed, the cross-talk normalization is important for SNP
> genotyping, but I'm unsure whether its necessary/appropriate for total
> copy number analysis.

The allelic cross-talk model does actually correct for two things: 1)
cross-talk between the probe signals for the two alleles, and 2)
global offset ("background") in the probes signals.  Correcting for
offset in signals is always important as any offset will compress
log-ratios (in a non-linear way) whether it is copy-number ratios or
gene-expression ratios.  Correcting for cross talk is indeed less
important for total copy-number analysis compare to genotyping,
because it does "self-normalize" when the two alleles are summed.
However there will still be an effect if the crosstalk is not
symmetric between the two alleles.  I also think the
"self-normalization" will depend on the genotype.

By definition, crosstalk calibration applies only to SNP units, e.g.
it cannot be applied to exon arrays.  Thus, for exon arrays we cannot
(unfortunately) utilize the crosstalk model to estimate the global
offset.  Instead we have to turn to other offset models, e.g. the RMA-
and the gcRMA background models.  Personally, I find the latter to be
more ad hoc than the allelic crosstalk model where the offset is easy
to argue for and straightforward to see in an (PMA,PMB) scatter plot.

The reason for the CN example not including a cross-talk calibration
step was just to keep the example simple in order to focus on the CN
estimates.  When the CRMA model, which includes the crosstalk part, is
published there will probably also be a CRMA-explicit example on the
website.

Neither quantile normalization nor fragment-length normalization
corrects for offsets in signals.

Cheers

Henrik

>
> Thanks,
>
> Jeremy
>
>
> >
>

Hi Mark,

this certainly looks strange.  I will have to look at this later, but
a few comments for troubleshooting.

It could have to do with the fact that you change the CDF and that
some how the ProbeAffinityFile is using the wrong/original CDF.  That
would explain the "systematic effects", which I actually believe/hope
consists of the correct values but some how are offset across arrays.
For the units that give inconsistent probe affinities, could please
verify that the chip effects are consistent?  That would tell us if
there is a problem with the convergence of the PLM algorithm.

Cheers

Henrik

messages.body_plain:
Hi all.

Well, the answer is simple.  Sadly, it took me my whole day to figure
it out.

Basically, with the brainarray annotation, you can have a probe that
is part of several probesets.  Problem is, you may get a different
estimated probe affinity for a particular probe in the different
transcripts and when you try and write them to a file all at the
same, the indices clash (because you can only store 1 probe affinity
per probe!) and only one gets stored.

This explains why when I write the whole set of probe affinities to
file at one time, this problem occurs, but when I 'updateUnits' on a
single probeset, I read out the correct result.  Its so obvious
(well, it is now).  This also explains why the chip effects are
unaffected.

If you have non-overlapping probesets, there will be no problems,
which is why the 'core' human exon CDF that Ken created has no problems.

So, I will have to resort to an alternative approach than reading
from the probe affinity files for my application.

Mark

>
> Hi Henrik.
>
> I've added a page describing the 'HsEx10stv2_Hs_REFSEQ' cdf file,
> where they come from, how to get them, pitfalls, etc.
>
> http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/hsex10stv2-hs-refseq

Thanks.

>
> Ahh.  Unfortunately, the page got added as a main heading at the
> bottom of the page and for the life of me, I could not figure out how
> to put it under the "Documentation on chip types" heading.  Can you
> tell me how to do that?

It seems to be the rule that only group maintainers can reorder the
pages, but anyone can add/edit.  I've moved it so it is a subsection
of the HuEx-1_0-st chip type, because 'HsEx10stv2_Hs_REFSEQ' is CDF
and not a chip type by itself.

>
> As for the 'core' CDF, I think it doesn't have this problem because
> its organized into affy's "transcript clusters", which do not overlap.

I see.

Cheers

H

>
> Cheers,
> Mark
>
>
> On 27/07/2007, at 6:18 PM, Henrik Bengtsson wrote:
>
> >
> > Hi Mark,
> >
> > that was tricky, but it all make sense when you explain it.  I did not
> > know about this many-to-one mapping.
> >
> > When you say 'brainarray', does that refer to the HsEx10stv2_Hs_REFSEQ
> > CDF?  Btw, is that the name of the chip type?  Do you know if apples
> > to any of the other two exon arrays in Section "Documentation on chip
> > types";
> >
> >   http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web
> >
> > Would you mind adding 1) a new subsection for the 'HsEx10stv2...' chip
> > type, and 2) add some warning text reminding us of the problem.
> >
> > To solve the problem, we need to find another solution because using
> > CEL files requires a one-to-one mapping.
> >
> > Ken, could you please comment on all this?  Did you experience this?
> > Is it just a coincidence that the 'core' CDF does not have this
> > problem?
> >
> > Cheers
> >
> > Henrik
> >
> > On 7/27/07, Mark Robinson <mrob...@wehi.edu.au> wrote:
> >>
> >> Hi all.
> >>
> >> Well, the answer is simple.  Sadly, it took me my whole day to figure
> >> it out.
> >>
> >> Basically, with the brainarray annotation, you can have a probe that
> >> is part of several probesets.  Problem is, you may get a different
> >> estimated probe affinity for a particular probe in the different
> >> transcripts and when you try and write them to a file all at the
> >> same, the indices clash (because you can only store 1 probe affinity
> >> per probe!) and only one gets stored.
> >>
> >> This explains why when I write the whole set of probe affinities to
> >> file at one time, this problem occurs, but when I 'updateUnits' on a
> >> single probeset, I read out the correct result.  Its so obvious
> >> (well, it is now).  This also explains why the chip effects are
> >> unaffected.
> >>
> >> If you have non-overlapping probesets, there will be no problems,
> >> which is why the 'core' human exon CDF that Ken created has no
> >> problems.
> >>
> >> So, I will have to resort to an alternative approach than reading
> >> from the probe affinity files for my application.
> >>
> >> Mark
> >>
> >>
> >>
> >>
> >> On 27/07/2007, at 11:56 AM, Mark Robinson wrote:
> >>
> >>>
> >>> Hi folks.
> >>>
> >>> A bit stumped here.
> >>>
> >>> If I fit the PLM on the whole set of units (I've picked
> >>> units=20790:56283 here since the brainarray CDF has 20789 single
> >>> probe units which I think are control probes?), and I pull out the
> >>> probe effects for the 5th one (z[[5]] below), it gives me probe
> >>> effects which sum to -5.009.  If I pull out the data (yy below), and
> >>> call 'fitUnit' for this object and use 'updateUnits' to write it to
> >>> the probeAffinities.cel file, it gets a set of probe affinities that
> >>> basically sum to 0 (some roundoff).  The chip effects are basically
> >>> unchanged either way, so there is no problem with the fits
> >>> themselves.
> >>>
> >>> I have played a bit with 'updateUnits' but haven't figured out
> >>> why it
> >>> writes something differently when you call on all units compared
> >>> with
> >>> a single unit.  Could be something in 'readUnits' too, I dunno.
> >>>
> >>> Still looking, but if anyone has any suggestions, I'm all ears.
> >>>
> >>> Mark
> >>>
> >>>
> >>>
> >>>
> >>>> fit(plm,units=20790:56283,force=T,verbose=verbose)
> >>> (... removed ...)
> >>>> ces<-getChipEffectSet(plm)
> >>>> pes<-getProbeAffinities(plm)
> >>>> x<-readUnits(csN,units=20790:56283)
> >>>> y<-readUnits(ces,units=20790:56283)
> >>>> z<-readUnits(pes,units=20790:56283)
> >>>> sum(log2(z[[5]][[1]]$phi))
> >>> [1] -5.009063
> >>>> yy<-readUnits(plm,units=20794)
> >>>> zz<-readUnits(pes,units=20794)
> >>>> plot(x[[5]][[1]]$inten[,1],yy[[1]][[1]]$intens[,1]); abline(0,1)
> >>> # these are equal
> >>>> fitUnit<-getFitUnitFunction(plm)
> >>>> fit<-lapply(yy,FUN=fitUnit)
> >>>> sum(fit[[1]][[1]]$theta-y[[5]][[1]]$theta) # very small - chip
> >>> effects are equal.
> >>> [1] -9.617917e-05
> >>>> sum(log2(z[[5]][[1]]$phi))
> >>> [1] -5.009063
> >>>> sum(log2(fit[[1]][[1]]$phi))
> >>> [1] 5.386316e-16
> >>>>
> >>>> paf<-getProbeAffinityFile(plm)
> >>>> updateUnits(paf,units=20794,data=fit,verbose=verbose)
> >>> Updating units...
> >>> Encoding units...
> >>> Encoding units...done
> >>> Updating units...done
> >>>> z<-readUnits(pes,units=20790:56283)
> >>>> sum(log2(z[[5]][[1]]$phi))
> >>> [1] 3.846865e-07
> >>>
> >>>
> >>>>>>>>> library(aroma.affymetrix)
> >>>>>>>>> name<-"Hodgson_GBM"
> >>>>>>>>> chipType <- "HsEx10stv2_Hs_REFSEQ"
> >>>>>>>>> cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name,
> >>>>>>>>> chipType=chipType,checkChipType=F)
> >>>>>>>>> cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType)
> >>>>>>>>> setCdf(cs, cdf)
> >>>>>>>>> qn <- QuantileNormalization(cs, typesToUpdate="pm")
> >>>>>>>>> csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose)
> >>>>>>>>> plm <- RmaPlm(csN)
> >>>>>>>>> fit(plm, verbose=verbose)
> >>>>>>>>> ces<-getChipEffectSet(plm)
> >>>>>>>>> pes<-getProbeAffinities(plm)
> >>>>>>>>> x<-readUnits(csN,units=20790:56283)
> >>>>>>>>> y<-readUnits(ces,units=20790:56283)
> >>>>>>>>> z<-readUnits(pes,units=20790:56283)
> >>>
> >>>
> >>>
> >>>
> >>>
> >>>>
> >>
> >>
> >>>
> >>
> >
> > >
>
>
> >
>
